context_pill: Diversion of Income vs Application of Income
example_summary: XYZ Ltd. purchased a sole-proprietorship subject to a sale deed condition to pay ₹ 15,000 p.a. to the proprietor's wife, which constitutes a diversion of income by overriding title.
source_provision:
| Parameter | Diversion of Income by Overriding Title | Application of Income |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage of Obligation** | Obligation attaches **before** income reaches or accrues to the assessee. | Obligation arises **after** income has reached or accrued to the assessee. |
| **Attachment Point** | Directly attached to the **source of income** or condition of title transfer. | Attached to the **assessee personally** or post-taxable profit application. |
| **Legal Consequence** | Income never forms part of assessee's Total Income (**Excluded**). | Income forms part of assessee's Total Income (**Fully Taxable**). |
| **Judicial Test** | Does the third party have an independent, enforceable paramount title on source? | Is the assessee merely applying their accrued net profit to discharge a liability? |


**Key Statutory Benchmarks for Diversion of Income**

* **Paramount Obligation at Acquisition**: Where an obligation to pay a third party is incorporated as an integral condition in the deed of transfer/purchase of a business or asset, it creates an overriding charge at source.

* **Charge on Source vs Personal Covenant**: If the payment obligation is secured directly against the income-generating source or net profits as a prerequisite condition of ownership, it constitutes a valid diversion by overriding title.


> [!IMPORTANT] Judicial Precedent Benchmark: Jit & Pal X-Rays (P.) Ltd. v. CIT (2004)
> When a business undertaking is acquired subject to a pre-existing charge or an overriding obligation stipulated in the acquisition deed itself, the amount diverted to the beneficiary under such overriding charge is diverted before it reaches the transferee. Consequently, it cannot be taxed in the hands of the transferee company.

director.justification: The question hinges on applying judicial precedent from Jit & Pal X-Rays (P.) Ltd. to determine whether an obligation under a sale deed is a diversion of income by overriding title or an application of income.
director.visual_metaphor: A main income stream diverted at the source gate before reaching the company's central reservoir.
